title: A projective fourfold with large fundamental group and non-Stein universal cover
main_claim: There is a smooth projective fourfold X containing a simple abelian surface A with im(pi_1(A)->pi_1(X)) = Z, such that X has large fundamental group but its universal cover is not Stein. This would give a counterexample to the Shafarevich holomorphic-convexity conjecture. The proof reduces to embedding a simple abelian surface A in a smooth projective S' with infinite cyclic pi_1-image. That embedding comes from an arithmetic ball-quotient arrangement with dihedral local covers and a local-to-global "path criterion" in hyperbolic reading graphs.

issues.description: Not an error, but it affects how much the argument rests on each part. The uniform hyperbolicity of the chart graphs D_v (P3) comes almost for free: each graph is quasi-isometric to a cone over a bounded metric space, so it is hyperbolic whatever the translation labels are. Because of this, the infinite-order conclusion rests entirely on the abstract local path criterion (Lemma thm:path-lemma) together with the prefix-compatibility (P2) check in Lemma app:chart-axioms. I re-derived both and found no failing step. Still, they are new and carry all the weight, which makes them the natural first target for a formal check.
issues.evidence: 'Hyperbolicity of the cone and quasi-isometry invariance ... prove hyperbolicity of the model graph'; the only lower-bound input is 'a single edge loop with distinct read endpoints represents a nonidentity element of pi_1(S)' (app:detection).

issues.location: Sec 3, 'Calculations within one chart', distance-transport paragraph (03-paths.tex)
issues.description: Several range conditions are stated tersely, for example the condition for transporting distances (|p|<=N/2, 2|a|+|b|<=N/2) and the claim that every chart calculation uses paths shorter than 1000k. I checked them against the constants H=1000*Delta, L>=10^6*H, k=20L, N>=10^5*k, and every later use stays inside the stated bounds. I am listing this only as a place where a referee would want explicit bookkeeping. It is not a gap.
issues.evidence: 'These bounds, as well as their versions with a,b interchanged, hold in every use below.'

coverage: I read all seven sections in build/sections. Sec 2: checked the codimension count for smoothness along F (rank c+2 bundle, degeneracy codimension 3 > 2), the interpolation lemma, the strict incidence count 4d+6 < 4c = 4d+8, the largeness cases, and the H_3 obstruction on C^2/K. Sec 3: re-derived the narrowing, extension and invariant constructions, including invariance under relations and the final strip calculation that forces [e]_v = d_v. Sec 4: checked the intersection inequalities by hand (c^2/a < 0.81 so red slopes meet the coupling hyperplanes and blue ones do not, 2c^2 > a), the meaning of the Gram-matrix exactness, the branching rules, F* = C x C, and the s-action eigenvalues on the fixed curves. Sec 5: checked the dihedral gluing with the coupling square roots (|z1| < sqrt(a/2) < c where |lambda| > 1), extension of the labels across the fillings, the buffer bound (sqrt(1-0.85^2)/0.85 = 0.6197 < 0.7), the kernel-compatibility cases, the sign consistency of l_z o s_* = l_w (via s^2 = id on F*), descent of the sum cover, and the cone hyperbolicity argument. Sec 6: checked the cyclic upper bound (k h_i = 1, k^2 = 1, h5 h6 = 1), the chart axioms P1-P2 in the individual/individual, central/central and mixed cases, the subdivision and meridian relations (including fixed loci and the resolution divisors), and that the pushed loop has l_w = 0 and l_z != 0. Sec 7: checked eigenspace codimension for the projective-bundle realization, the Hamm-Le plus Ehresmann argument, the small resolution charts, the normal-bundle adjustment, the Nakai-Moishezon lemma, the restriction O_G(0, beta-alpha), and the downward H^1 vanishing. I did not independently verify cited external theorems (Stover-Toledo/Llosa Isenrich-Py, Zarhin, Hamm-Le). I did not look for counterexamples to Lemma 3.1 beyond small toy cases.
sibling_notes: The board already had an earlier rank-88 entry for this same paper (verdict no_gap_found). That entry said the Sec 3 local path criterion had not been fully re-derived. I focused this pass on that gap and on the P2 chart compatibility it depends on. I re-derived both and found no failing step, so this pass agrees with the earlier verdict.
